Workers at the Hunterian Museum packing up some of the 3,000 human skulls stored in a shed for their transfer to the Natural History Museum. London. 1948.

The Hunterian Museum is part of England's Royal College Of Surgeons. The Museum's vast collections of human remains stem from centuries of exploration and colonization. These items were used to study differences in human populations and the origin of the human species, with items from overseas being brought back only if they were “rare or unusual specimens… for their curiosity value as well as for research”. Note that each skull has a serial/catalog number on the forehead. Since the 1990s many Western countries have implemented laws to return the human remains from former colonies or conquered people.
